answer: A place I would love to visit again is Darjeeling, a small hill town in India, which I went to a few years ago and which completely charmed me. I first went there with two friends from university just after our final exams, crossing the border by land and taking a shared jeep up the winding mountain roads. I only stayed a few days, which was nowhere near long enough to appreciate it fully. The town was wonderfully [[picturesque]], with steep lanes, old colonial buildings and tea gardens clinging to the hillsides, and on clear mornings we could see the snowy Himalayan peaks in the distance. On that first visit I explored the local trails, rode the famous toy train for a short stretch and sampled the regional food, especially the momos, but I feel I only [[scratched the surface]]. What draws me back is the incredibly [[tranquil]] pace of life there, which was a world away from my hectic routine. There is a certain [[magnetic]] quality to some places that stays with you long after you leave, and this town has it. I have often found myself daydreaming about returning and staying longer next time, perhaps in spring when the views are clearer. I would also like to take my parents, because my father loves tea and would enjoy visiting a proper tea estate. Honestly, some destinations simply leave you wanting more, and revisiting it would be a genuine [[delight]]. I hope to make it happen soon.

followUps.q: What would you do differently next time?
followUps.answer: I would stay much longer, at least a week, and go in spring when the views are clearer. I would also like to stay in a small family-run guesthouse rather than a hotel.

followUps.q: Do you prefer visiting new places or returning to familiar ones?
followUps.answer: Generally I prefer new places, because I love discovering something different. But a few special places, like Darjeeling, are worth returning to, because you notice things you missed the first time.
